tests.title: Named returns the requested tools in names order, matches only top-level tools and prefers the first of two same-named tools
given: a set ts of tools read_file, write_file, list_files in that order
a wrapper tool in ts whose ReachableTools hold a tool named hidden
two tools in a second set both named dup, with different Descriptions
tests.when: Named(ts, "list_files", "read_file") is called, then Named(ts, "hidden"), then Named(dupSet, "dup")
then: the first call returns exactly two tools with Names list_files, read_file in that order and a nil error
the second call returns a nil slice and a non-nil error because ReachableTools are not searched
the third call returns the first dup tool (its Description matches the first)
tests.pseudocode: got, err = core.Named(ts, 'list_files', 'read_file'); assert err == nil; assert names(got) == ['list_files','read_file']; _, err = core.Named(ts, 'hidden'); assert err != nil; d, _ = core.Named(dupSet, 'dup'); assert d[0].Description == first.Description

tests.title: Named returns a fresh slice of value copies that does not alias ts
given: a set ts of three tools with distinct Descriptions
tests.when: Named(ts, "read_file") is called and the result's element Description and the result slice are then overwritten
then: ts[i].Description is unchanged for every i
appending to the result does not change ts
the result's backing array differs from ts's (&got[0] != &ts[idx])
tests.pseudocode: got,_ = Named(ts,'read_file'); got[0].Description='x'; assert ts[0].Description == orig; assert &got[0] != &ts[0]

tests.title: Named with no names returns an empty non-nil slice and a nil error
given: a non-empty tool set, and separately a nil tool set
tests.when: Named(ts) and Named(nil) are called with no names
then: each result is non-nil with length 0
each error is nil
tests.pseudocode: got, err = Named(ts); assert got != nil && len(got)==0 && err == nil; got, err = Named(nil); assert got != nil && len(got)==0 && err == nil

tests.title: Named reports every missing name and the names the set holds
given: a set ts of read_file and write_file in that order
an empty tool set
tests.when: Named(ts, "no_such_tool") is called; then Named(ts, "write_file", "b_missing", "a_missing"); then Named(empty, "x")
then: the first error text equals `core: no tool named "no_such_tool"; the set holds: read_file, write_file` and the tools are nil
the second error begins "core: ", quotes "b_missing" before "a_missing" (names order) and lists read_file before write_file
the third error begins "core: ", quotes "x" and states that the set is empty
the returned tools are nil in all three calls
tests.pseudocode: got, err = Named(ts,'no_such_tool'); assert got == nil; assert err.Error() == 'core: no tool named "no_such_tool"; the set holds: read_file, write_file'; assert index(err2,'"b_missing"') < index(err2,'"a_missing"')

tests.title: Named rejects a name repeated in names and quotes the first repeated name
given: a set ts holding read_file, write_file and list_files
tests.when: Named(ts, "read_file", "write_file", "write_file", "read_file") is called
then: the tools are nil
the error is non-nil, begins "core: " and quotes "write_file" (the first repeated name), not "read_file"
tests.pseudocode: got, err = Named(ts,'read_file','write_file','write_file','read_file'); assert got == nil; assert hasPrefix(err,'core: ') && contains(err,'"write_file"')

tests.title: Named returns tools matching any sequence of distinct names from ts, and is race-free under concurrent calls
given: a generated tool set ts with distinct names
tests.when: for any ts and any sequence of distinct names drawn from ts's Names, Named is called once sequentially and then concurrently from several goroutines on the same ts
then: the returned Names equal the requested sequence
every concurrent result equals the sequential result
the race detector reports nothing (go test -race)
tests.pseudocode: for ts, picks in gen(): got,_ = Named(ts,picks...); assert names(got)==picks; parallel(8): assert names(Named(ts,picks...))==picks

tests.title: Allow decides exactly as Restricted with AllowedPrograms for any programs and any context
given: guard.Restricted(Options{AllowedPrograms: programs}) as the oracle
tests.when: for any program list (including empty) and any tool-call context (execute or run_command with a generated command string, or a non-shell tool), both guards are called
then: Block, Reason and Terminate are equal field by field
every blocked Reason begins "guard.Restricted: "
tests.pseudocode: a = Allow(progs...); r = Restricted(Options{AllowedPrograms: progs}); for ctx in gen(): da=a(ctx); dr=r(ctx); assert da == dr

tests.title: Mutating the caller's slice after Allow returns does not change decisions
given: programs := []string{"ls", "cat"} with spare capacity
a guard built by Allow(programs...)
tests.when: the caller overwrites programs[1] with "rm", appends "curl" and reorders, then the guard is called for rm, curl, ls and cat commands via execute
then: rm and curl remain blocked
ls and cat remain allowed
tests.pseudocode: g = Allow(progs...); progs[1]='rm'; progs = append(progs,'curl'); assert g(exec('rm x')).Block; assert g(exec('curl u')).Block; assert !g(exec('ls')).Block; assert !g(exec('cat f')).Block

tests.title: Allow with no programs blocks every shell call and allows other tools
given: g := guard.Allow()
tests.when: g is called for execute and run_command with benign commands, and for read_file and an unknown tool name
then: execute and run_command decisions have Block=true
read_file and the unknown tool have Block=false
tests.pseudocode: g=Allow(); assert g(ctx('execute','ls')).Block; assert g(ctx('run_command','ls')).Block; assert !g(ctx('read_file',...)).Block

tests.title: faux.ToolCall panics with a message naming faux.ToolCall, id and tool name when args is not an object

tests.title: A faux.Provider scripted with the helpers emits the same events as with the literals
given: a real faux.Provider A scripted with faux.ToolCall(...) then faux.Text(...)
a real faux.Provider B scripted with the equivalent one-block Turn literals

tests.pseudocode: evA = collect(faux.New(ToolCall(..),Text(..))) per call; evB = collect(faux.New(literal1, literal2)); assert DeepEqual(evA, evB)

tests.title: Open calls Create, Sync, Tools once each in order, returns the unwrapped sandbox and never closes it
given: a test double Provider and Sandbox in package sandbox_test that records calls and their contexts
a non-nil Source (LocalDir) and ToolOptions{SpillDir: "/abs"}
a ctx carrying a value
tests.when: sandbox.Open(ctx, p, spec, src, opts) is called
then: the recorded order is Create, Sync, Tools, each once
Create received spec and ctx; Sync received src; Tools received opts
the returned Sandbox is identical (==) to the one Create returned
the returned proxies are the slice Tools returned
the error is nil
Close was called zero times
tests.pseudocode: sb, tools, err = Open(ctx,p,spec,src,opts); assert p.calls==['Create','Sync','Tools']; assert sb == p.created; assert p.created.closeCalls == 0

tests.title: Open with a nil src skips Sync
given: a recording test double Provider and Sandbox
tests.when: sandbox.Open(ctx, p, spec, nil, opts) is called
then: the recorded calls are Create then Tools, with no Sync
the returned sandbox and proxies are those the double produced and the error is nil
tests.pseudocode: Open(ctx,p,spec,nil,opts); assert p.calls==['Create','Tools']

tests.title: Open on local with a LocalDir returns a live sandbox whose proxies match Sandbox.Tools
given: the local provider (local.Unisolated) with TMPDIR set to a temp dir (skipped on Windows)
a host directory with src/main.go containing known text
tests.when: sandbox.Open(ctx, p, spec, sandbox.LocalDir{Path: dir}, sandbox.ToolOptions{}) is called, then the read_file proxy is executed, then Tools with equal options, a second Sync, Export and Close are called
then: Open returns a nil error and a non-nil sandbox
the proxy Names equal the Names a later sb.Tools call with equal options returns, in the same order
the read_file proxy output contains the synced file's content
the second Sync, Export to a host dir and Close all succeed
tests.pseudocode: sb, tl, err = Open(...); assert err==nil; assert names(tl)==names(sb.Tools(ctx,ToolOptions{})); out = find(tl,'read_file').Execute(ctx,{path:'src/main.go'}); assert contains(out, text); assert sb.Sync(...)==nil; assert sb.Export(...)==nil; assert sb.Close(ctx)==nil

tests.title: Open with a nil Provider returns a sandbox-prefixed error without panicking

tests.title: Open returns Create's error unchanged and calls no Sandbox method

tests.title: A failing Sync or Tools closes the sandbox once and returns the step error unchanged
given: a test double whose Sync fails with error S in one case and whose Tools fails with error T in another
Close succeeds in both
tests.when: sandbox.Open is called in each case
then: Close was called exactly once
the result is (nil, nil, err) with err == S in the Sync case and err == T in the Tools case
in the Sync case Tools was never called
tests.pseudocode: for step in [Sync,Tools]: sb,tl,err = Open(...); assert sb==nil && tl==nil; assert err == stepErr; assert double.closeCalls == 1

tests.title: A step failure plus a Close failure returns errors.Join matching both

then: sandbox and tools are nil

errors.Is(err, C) is true
Close was called once
tests.pseudocode: sb,tl,err = Open(...); assert errors.Is(err,S) && errors.Is(err,C); assert closeCalls==1

tests.title: Cleanup runs with an uncancelled context carrying the original values when ctx is already cancelled

a test double whose Sync fails and whose Close records ctx.Err() and ctx.Value(key)

the step error is returned (errors.Is matches it)
tests.pseudocode: ctx,cancel = WithCancel(WithValue(bg,k,'v')); cancel(); _,_,err = Open(ctx,...); assert double.closeErr == nil && double.closeVal=='v'; assert errors.Is(err, S)

tests.title: Open's error matches every sentinel the failing step matches, with or without a Close failure
given: a test double with a configurable failing step (Sync or Tools), a step error wrapping a sentinel, and a Close that succeeds or fails

errors.Is(err, X) is true
when Close failed, errors.Is(err, closeErr) is also true
tests.pseudocode: for step,X,closeFails in gen(): stepErr = fmt.Errorf('ctx: %w',X); _,_,err = Open(...); assert errors.Is(err,X)
